subject: snail
pitch: A garden snail on an adventure. A glossy spiral shell striped in caramel, chocolate and cream, a soft grey-green body with a pebbly texture and a slimy shine, two long eye stalks with little black eyes and two short feelers below. A tiny ladybird hitches a ride on top of the shell.
reasoning:
I'm sizing a realistic snail model—roughly 10cm body length with a 4.5cm shell—then starting to plan the skeleton structure, beginning with the root foot joint.

Now I'm working out the body chain geometry, running a path from tail to head with rising neck curvature, and sketching jaw/lip details for the mouth. I'm also deciding on coloring: a mottled grey-green base with pebbly patches and a lighter countershaded belly to make the skin look organic.

I'm considering adjusting material roughness across all meshes to get that slimy, slightly glossy sheen, traversing the root node and setting roughness uniformly since materials are shared by color. Now I'm figuring out how to build the shell as a tapering spiral tube, thinking through the right axis orientation so it coils naturally against the snail's back.

For the spiral geometry itself, I'm working out radius decay from a wide outer opening down to a tight inner point across about 2.5 turns, balancing tube thickness against whorl spacing so adjacent coils don't overlap or leave ugly gaps.

I'm placing the shell opening near the front-bottom of the body so the starting tube radius tucks inside the body mesh without poking through, then working out the right-hand spiral direction starting from that bottom point.

I'm sizing the shell as a planispiral, like a nautilus though a real garden snail's is more conical—using pitch 0.007 along the x-axis with the spiral centered to keep tube width and body proportions roughly matched. Checking the math, the shell's overall diameter comes out close to 0.093 against the body's length, which seems reasonably in line with real snail proportions where the shell is roughly half the extended body length.

I rework the radius down to 0.022 with a tube factor of 0.5 for an ~0.066 diameter shell, repositioning the center so the shell sits between roughly y=0.04 and y=0.073, leaving room for eye stalks up to 0.08 against a 0.12 body length—this feels better scaled, though I note the apex tapering thin while the whorls widen going outward.

For coloring, I'm planning to paint stripes that run lengthwise along the spiral's tube direction (matching real snail shell banding) by mapping angular position into 40-degree bands cycling through caramel, chocolate, and cream tones, with a thin chocolate accent woven in.

Now I'm refining that paint function: I'm bucketing the angle into 30-degree segments mapped to a repeating caramel/chocolate/cream palette, and layering in darker growth-line bands at regular intervals along the spiral length using a fractional threshold check. I also want a small torus at the shell's opening to act as a lip, oriented along the spiral's starting tangent with a thin tube radius, plus I'm considering how to sprout the eye stalks from the head area.

Now I'm designing the eye stalks and feelers as bone chains: curved catmull paths rising outward from the head with tapering sweep radii and body coloring, each ending in a small black eye sphere with a tiny white glint, while the feelers follow a shorter, lower, forward-pointing path with fewer joints, all tagged under a "tentacle" role.

For the head and jaw, I'm extending the body spine chain to end in a head joint, then adding a child jaw joint positioned slightly forward-down from it to support upper and lower lip parts for the mouth.

Still shaping body proportions...

Since the tapered tail makes a constant path height awkward, I'll shift the y-coordinate downward by the difference between a baseline radius and the tapered radius, keeping the first few points at a fixed height before transitioning.

Writing path coordinates...

Still defining radius taper...

Working through the spiral radius decay as it winds around, estimating the shell's top extent at roughly 0.064 by tracking how the whorl shrinks each half-turn — the outer pass dominates the top while the initial pass sets the bottom extent, giving an asymmetric spiral silhouette typical of a shell.

For placing the ladybird, I'll cast a ray downward against the shell surface near a point close to the top, or just use nearest-point lookup to find a solid hit location and its normal, then build the ladybird body (dome, dots, head, legs, wing-split line) oriented upright at that hit point.

Adding spots as small spheres, a thin center line, and tiny antennae rods while skipping legs. I'm working out where to anchor the shell joint and probing the snail's surface to figure out the correct top-facing orientation and lateral center for placement.

Building the ladybird's dome body and seam line...

Working out the gap between the two red hemisphere offsets, trying small x-offsets to find a spacing where they don't overlap the black body beneath but still show a thin seam at center.

Now I'm adding small black dots for spots, computing their positions on the surface of each red ellipsoid so they sit correctly on the curved dome.

Adding tiny white face dots, antennae rods, and small crawling legs made of thin black cylinders beneath the body, then considering scaling the whole ladybird down slightly for proportion.

Now I'm working out the eyes with black spheres and tiny white glint highlights, placed at the tips of curved eye-stalks built from chained bone segments that taper from thicker base to narrower tip.

I'm positioning the feeler stalks with their own curved paths and tapering radii, making sure they attach near the top of the head sphere, then setting up the body chain with tail, hips, chest, and head joints linked to the root.

Now I'm adding the jaw joint near the mouth position at the front-bottom of the head, checking that it sits within the head sphere's radius so it doesn't poke outside the geometry.

Working out the mouth details: a lower lip sphere flattened and positioned to protrude slightly past the head bulb, plus a tiny upper lip bump near the snout, and a small dark flattened sphere for the mouth line between them, all attached to the jaw and head bones.

Now I'm designing the shell's spiral opening — placing the start point of the shell curve relative to a center offset, and deciding how to cap it so the opening reads as a round aperture facing forward. I'm setting up a lip torus at the start point, oriented so its ring sits in the plane perpendicular to the tangent direction, matching the shell's forward-facing opening.

I'm also checking whether the shell's start position is centered relative to the body — since the spiral's center point sits offset in x, I need to adjust that offset so the tube's cross-section spans a reasonable range without looking lopsided against the body.

Defining shell band colors...

I'm worried the clock-based banding referenced to world-up won't stay consistent around the coil—since the outer/inner side flips between top and bottom of the spiral, the stripes could appear to twist or jump discontinuously rather than wrapping cleanly along the tube.

Rather than tracking exact axis geometry, I think a simpler approximation works: since the coil's axis effect is small locally, I can just use constant-x bands as stripes around the tube, which will roughly align with latitude lines along the whorl direction.

Working out the arc-length parametrization properly, I realize for a logarithmic spiral the radius varies linearly with arclength fraction, so I can compute the angular fraction from the log ratio of radii and use that to locate the tube center, then derive stripe latitude from the x-offset relative to that center.

Picking colored bands across the stripe width now...

Still computing taper and tube radius...

Still shaping tail taper and shift function, then setting up the sweep call with the radius function and skin color, and sketching a scaled countershaded pebble pattern for the paint.

I'm skipping the slime trail idea as too costly, and now writing the head sphere part attached to the body with its scale and position parameters.

I need the shell joint bone for ladybird parts, pulling the attachment point from a surface hit so I can anchor geometry there, and I'll pre-scale geometries directly rather than relying on a scale parameter to avoid bugs.

Still building ladybird parts...
